recommendation: Keep the commit as-is for FHIR-7933. It removes stale optional-request wording while aligning the HTTP page with current Bundle invariants. Review the separate FHIR-34388 versus FHIR-19620 PATCH wording conflict under that issue family if assigned.
issue_request: FHIR-7933 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1 and asked to remove the then-current requirement that every history entry contain entry.transaction, because servers can create resource versions through channels other than FHIR REST interactions.
initial_application: SVN revision 5343, represented by git commit 8c21b3c5922f5f25a417a49d45e55c38a880f81e, updated source/http.html to allow a history entry to contain either resource state or transaction details for a DELETE. Later source history renamed transaction to request, but the optional-request paragraph remained and eventually became incomplete and inconsistent with current Bundle constraints.
additional_context: FHIR-8818 renamed the old transaction element to request. FHIR-17075 later clarified that history Bundles need request/response details, and FHIR-38942 moved Bundle type requirements into invariants; current Bundle bdl-3b requires history entries to contain request and response elements. FHIR-19620 says PATCH interactions are represented as PUT in history and adds bdl-14 prohibiting PATCH request methods. A 2020 implementers Zulip thread clarified that non-REST changes should still be exposed with equivalent create/update/delete request details.
reconciliation: Updated the active source/http.html history interaction paragraph to require request and response elements, explain equivalent request details for changes outside the RESTful interface, and require a resource for PUT/POST while noting DELETE history entries omit the resource.
source_changes: source/http.html: revised the history interaction paragraph to require request and response details and describe equivalent non-REST request details.

related_jiras.note: Renamed the old Bundle transaction element to request, explaining the current terminology used in source/http.html.
Later Published issue clarified that request/response details are mandatory for history Bundles, superseding the optional-request reading of the 2015 FHIR-7933 application.
Moved Bundle entry requirements into invariants, including the current bdl-3b request/response rule for history.
Clarified that PATCH interactions are represented as PUT in history and added the bdl-14 PATCH prohibition, supporting the decision not to add PATCH to this paragraph.
Later PATCH wording was applied to Bundle notes but conflicts with bdl-14; this was noted but not decided for the FHIR-7933 seed.
